newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - November 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - November 27.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Sri Lankan Foreign Minister Lakshman Kadirgamar says French government is not supportive of the LTTE (Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam). He accompanied President Kumaratunga on her official visit to France.
More than 10,000 Army deserters return in response to the recently announced general amnesty, defence sources say.
Government paramedics work-to-rule campaign costs state 250,000 rupees daily for medical tests done at private nursing homes.
Shell warns dealers against hoarding of gas cylinders, and seeks public help to prevent black marketeering.
The LTTE lost 11,860 fighters in confrontations with Sri Lankan forces up to October 31, 1996, in the separatist war now in its 14th year, says Tiger Radio.
Government to introduce a new pensions scheme from December 17, 1996 as part of its public sector reforms programme.
Four youths rob a People's Bank branch in the Maharagama area close to Colombo, and make off with nearly 800,000 rupees, Police sources say.
